description: GAMA is an open-source modelling and simulation environment for building spatially explicit agent-based simulations. Modellers write models in its own language, GAML, load GIS data such as shapefiles, OpenStreetMap extracts and rasters, and run, visualise and explore them in a desktop environment or in batch mode. The provider is the GAMA Platform open-source project, which runs community mailing lists and the GAMA Days meeting (online in November 2026). Coverage is generic and worldwide: the platform has no built-in domain, and the lead that brought it here came from searches for emergency evacuation and hospital infection models built with it. The Java code is on GitHub under the GNU GPL version 3; releases come bundled with a Java runtime, the latest tag read today is 2026.09.0, and commits continued in September 2026. Caveats: GAMA supplies the engine and language, not validated models, so every application needs its own calibration; large models need tuning for performance. Simulation uses: evacuation of a city or building under a hazard, spread of infection among patients and staff in a hospital, and interactions between traffic, shelters and emergency vehicles in a disaster. Related records: JuPedSim (model-jupedsim) models pedestrian evacuation in detail, and MATSim (model-matsim) simulates transport demand at city scale.
